# Conventions and a working dictionary {#sec-conventions}

This appendix is part of the derivation, not just typography. When comparing with another source, first match its jump normalization, field rotation, Fourier convention, and definition of $G^K$.

## Units, operators, and rates

We set $\hbar=k_B=1$. A Hamiltonian has units of frequency; time has inverse-frequency units. Bosonic operators obey $[a,a^\dagger]=1$ and continuum fields obey $[\hat\psi(\mathbf x),\hat\psi^\dagger(\mathbf x')]=\delta^{(d)}(\mathbf x-\mathbf x')$. Thus the continuum field has units length$^{-d/2}$.

Our dissipator is

$$
\mathcal D[L]\rho=L\rho L^\dagger-\frac12\{L^\dagger L,\rho\}.
$$ {#eq-dictionary-dissipator}

A term $\kappa\mathcal D[a]$ gives $\partial_t\langle a\rangle=-\kappa\langle a\rangle/2$ and $\partial_t\langle a^\dagger a\rangle=-\kappa\langle a^\dagger a\rangle$ in the absence of other terms. Some literature instead writes $\kappa(2a\rho a^\dagger-\{a^\dagger a,\rho\})$. Its $\kappa$ equals our $\kappa/2$. Check a pole or a number-decay equation before comparing formulas.

With pump $p\mathcal D[a^\dagger]$, define

$$
\Gamma=\frac{\kappa-p}{2},\qquad
\partial_t\langle n\rangle=-(\kappa-p)\langle n\rangle+p.
$$ {#eq-dictionary-linewidth}

The linear model has a normalizable stationary state only when $\kappa>p$. At equality its occupation grows without bound; above equality a nonlinear saturation is required.

## Fields and contours

The independent integration variables on the forward and backward branches are $\phi_\pm,\bar\phi_\pm$. Bars label the complex partner in the coherent-state integral. At a physical saddle they are complex conjugates; variations treat them as independent.

$$
\phi_c=\frac{\phi_++\phi_-}{\sqrt2},\qquad
\phi_q=\frac{\phi_+-\phi_-}{\sqrt2},\qquad
\psi=\frac{\phi_c}{\sqrt2}\quad\text{at }\phi_q=0.
$$ {#eq-dictionary-rotation}

The last equality identifies the physical amplitude, so a physical density $|\psi|^2$ corresponds to $|\phi_c|^2/2$. Effective-action chapters may use an explicitly defined $\rho=\bar\phi_c\phi_c$; this $\rho$ is twice the physical mean-field density. Coefficients must be translated with the field definition.

We write $Z=\int\mathcal D\phi\,e^{iS}$ and $W=-i\log Z$. A positive noise term in the action has the form $+iD|\phi_q|^2$ with $D\geq0$; it suppresses nonzero response histories because $i(iD)=-D$. At zero sources $Z=1$ for a normalized initial density matrix. The bulk action vanishes at coincident histories. A boundary functional still carries the initial state.

## Fourier transforms and the Keldysh matrix

The convention is

$$
f(t,\mathbf x)=\int\frac{d\omega}{2\pi}\frac{d^d k}{(2\pi)^d}
 e^{-i\omega t+i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}f(\omega,\mathbf k).
$$ {#eq-dictionary-fourier}

For bosons,

$$
\begin{split}
G^R(t,t')&=-i\theta(t-t')\langle[a(t),a^\dagger(t')]\rangle,\\
G^A(t,t')&=+i\theta(t'-t)\langle[a(t),a^\dagger(t')]\rangle,\\
G^K(t,t')&=-i\langle\{a(t),a^\dagger(t')\}\rangle.
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-dictionary-green}

The matrix ordering is $(c,q)$:

$$
G=\begin{pmatrix}G^K&G^R\\G^A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
P=G^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&P^A\\P^R&P^K\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-dictionary-matrix}

Matrix multiplication includes integration over intermediate spacetime variables. For a stable pumped oscillator,

$$
P^R=\omega-\omega_0+i\Gamma,\quad
P^A=(P^R)^*,\quad P^K=i(\kappa+p),\qquad
G^K=-G^R P^K G^A.
$$ {#eq-dictionary-cavity}

Retarded poles lie below the real frequency axis for stable evolution. At equal time, $iG^K(t,t)=2\langle n\rangle+1$. Losing the $+1$ loses vacuum fluctuations.

For a Hermitian quadrature $X$, a common alternative symmetrized spectrum is $C_X(\omega)=\frac12\int dt\,e^{i\omega t}\langle\{X(t),X(0)\}\rangle$. With our definitions, $C_X=iG_X^K/2$. The susceptibility for a perturbation $+f(t)X$ is $G_X^R$; for $-h(t)X$ it is $-G_X^R$. An absorptive spectrum must be compared together with its coupling convention.

## Noise and classical fields

A complex noise $\zeta=\zeta_1+i\zeta_2$ is circular when $\langle\zeta\zeta\rangle=0$. If

$$
\langle\zeta^*(x)\zeta(x')\rangle=2\sigma\delta(x-x'),
$$ {#eq-dictionary-complex-noise}

then each real component has covariance $\sigma\delta(x-x')$. A real phase noise is often defined by $\langle\eta(x)\eta(x')\rangle=2\Delta\delta(x-x')$. These two definitions cannot be exchanged without projecting onto amplitude and phase and tracking their factors. The relevant chapters carry out that projection explicitly.

Itô and Stratonovich prescriptions agree for additive noise, but multiplicative noise can generate a drift correction. A continuum action derived from a discretized master equation inherits an ordering and equal-time prescription. One must not choose a different prescription halfway through a calculation.

## Notation across applications

| Symbol | Meaning and qualification |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal L$ | Liouvillian superoperator |
| $\Gamma_k$ | Scale-dependent one-particle-irreducible effective action; $k$ here is an RG scale |
| $\Gamma$ or $\gamma$ in a cavity calculation | A linewidth defined locally; never infer its relation to a jump rate from the symbol |
| $\rho_0$ | Condensate density in the field normalization specified in the chapter |
| $K_c,K_d$ | Coherent and dissipative gradient coefficients of the physical CGLE |
| $u_c,u_d$ | Coherent interaction and dissipative saturation coefficients |
| $D,\lambda,\Delta$ | Phase diffusion, nonlinear phase coupling, and phase-noise strength in KPZ |
| $\chi,z,\beta$ | Roughness, dynamic, and growth exponents, with $\beta=\chi/z$ |
| $n_q,\sigma_q$ in heating | Phonon occupation and positive on-shell linewidth, not a cavity density or noise variance |
| $q_{\mathrm{EA}}$ | Edwards-Anderson frozen correlation, not a quantum field |

All phase-only conclusions assume density modes have already relaxed. A low-energy phonon theory assumes a microscopic momentum cutoff and a time interval before injected energy invalidates that cutoff. Thermodynamic-limit claims and finite-size crossovers are distinguished in the application chapters.
